feature: Customer Portal v2 -- MICROSOFT CHANGES (/portal-v2/ms-changes), now reading the customer's REAL Microsoft 365 Message Center from GET /api/portal/message-center instead of the msChangesData.ts design fixture. Microsoft ships in waves; pick a wave and the page becomes that wave. The eleven-bucket density grid, the five wave bands, the stat cards, the workload rows, the post corpus and the scan time are all derived from the posts message-center-sync.ts pulls from Graph /admin/serviceAnnouncement/messages. This manifest proves the DOM shows what the ENDPOINT returned: every data value it asserts is EXTRACTED FROM THE API RESPONSE at run time and interpolated, so it cannot pass against a stale fixture and does not need re-pinning when Microsoft posts again.
notes: THE LOGIN BLOCK IS NOT OPTIONAL. /portal-v2/* sits behind ProtectedRoute.
UI ROUTE SHAPE: /portal/{slug}/portal-v2/ms-changes/{wave}. App.tsx declares '/portal-v2/ms-changes/:wave' BEFORE '/portal-v2/ms-changes', and both before '/portal-v2/:pillar'.
shaneapp://runTest hits the DEPLOYED build, not the local worktree.

WHY THE FIXTURE NUMBERS ARE GONE. The previous version pinned '35', '80' and '100' as the wave-band counts, and drove the post detail through the design's own post ids (MC1042318 / MC1049877) and its prose ('eleven accounts that authenticated over IMAP or SMTP AUTH', 'fails silently at 23:00'). Every one of those was a property of the DESIGN FIXTURE -- the prototype's fictional Halden Materials tenant -- and none survives the page reading a real Message Center. A run against real data proved it: the Late August band rendered 'LATE AUG 98' where the manifest demanded '35'. They are replaced by values extracted from the endpoint at run time, which is the pattern CLAUDE.md prescribes (apiTests + uiStep textContains) and is a STRONGER test, because it fails if the page falls back to the fixture -- something the old assertions could not detect.

WHAT IS REAL AND WHAT IS NOT, so a reader does not over-read a green run. REAL, and asserted from the API here: the post corpus and every post's title, Microsoft's own body text, the eleven-bucket axis and its dates, the density grid, the wave bands and their counts, the six stat cards, the workload rows, the item count and the sync time. NOT REAL, and deliberately left on the design fixture WHOLE rather than half-filled: the per-department impact groups (MSC20-21), the seen-in-the-wild list (MSC40-42), the landed-wave retrospective (MSC43-47), the named RACI owners, the tenant's change freezes and the wave notice. Those need a read of the customer's own configuration or a human write-up, and nothing in this build produces either for Message Center posts. The steps that touch them are still real assertions about what the page renders -- they are simply not evidence of live data, and are labelled FIXTURE so nobody reads them as such.

MSC5/MSC6 ARE THE LIVE-DATA PROOF, and the two steps to look at first if this manifest ever goes red. The source line renders 'Your Microsoft Message Center · {itemCount} posts · synced {scanAt}' ONLY when the hook actually received a scoped payload with posts; the fixture path renders the design's 'Read against your tenant · scanned 19 August, 08:04' instead. Asserting the EXTRACTED item count and sync time there means a silent fall back to the fixture fails the run rather than passing it quietly.

MSC16 DEPENDS ON THE TOP-SCORING POST BEING A RETIREMENT, and says so rather than hiding it. posts[] is sorted bucket-ascending then score-descending, so posts[0] is the highest-scoring post of the first wave; on this tenant it is a retirement, so it renders in 'What stops working' as pv2-msc-break-{id}. If a future sync makes the top post a decision instead, re-point MSC16-MSC19 at pv2-msc-queue-{{firstPostId}} -- the step is still asserting a REAL post either way.

MSC18 IS THE HONESTY ASSERTION. The tenant half of a post detail carries a STATED ABSENCE, not an invented count: nothing in this build reads the customer's configuration against a Message Center notice, so the page says so in the endpoint's own words. Asserting that copy pins the one thing that would be genuinely misleading if it ever changed -- a fixture's 'eleven accounts...' finding printed under a real customer's real post.

THE POST BUDGET IS SPENT PER WAVE, and MSC12 is the regression guard. A flat top-240 cap over a bucket-ordered list left the Q3 and Q4 waves with no posts at all on this tenant (449 land on the axis), so those waves rendered 'Nothing in this wave stops working here' over posts that exist and were simply not sent. MSC12 asserts a real post id in the LAST wave, which is exactly the case a flat cap breaks.
THERE IS NO NEGATIVE TEXT ASSERTION IN THIS HARNESS, and an array in textContains is ANY-of, not all-of. Every all-of assertion here is its own step.
NO `select` STEPS in the asserted flow. The forms' selects live in the right FormDrawer and are not driven here.

VERIFICATION: RUN GREEN 57/57 against the deployed build 56572b90, on the testbed customer's REAL Message Center -- 501 items, 449 of them on the twelve-month axis. The endpoint returned scoped:true with real Microsoft titles, real per-workload counts and a real sync time; the DOM was then asserted against those extracted values. The security shape was proved live alongside it: a token with no customer claim gets 403 'No customer identity on token', an anonymous call gets 401, and '?customerId=3' does not select another tenant (the route source contains no req.query at all).

THE REWRITE WAS PROMPTED BY A REAL FAILURE, not by inspection. The PREVIOUS version of this manifest was run against the same build and failed exactly where it should have: the Late August band rendered 'LATE AUG 98' against its hardcoded fixture '35'. That is what proved the page had genuinely moved onto live data, and it is the reason every data assertion here is now extracted at run time instead of typed.
ENV VARS required: DEPLOY_URL, TEST_PORTAL_EMAIL / TEST_PORTAL_PASSWORD.

apiTests.name: SETUP -- log in as the designated TESTBED account; extract the bearer.

API1 -- the NEW customer-scoped route exists, admits a CustomerUser, and resolved a tenant from the JWT rather than failing closed. `scoped:true` is the endpoint's own claim that it found this customer's tenant row.
API2 -- the tenant's Message Center is not empty, and the sync time is real; both are rendered on the page's source line.
API3 -- take the highest-scoring post of the first wave: its id drives the detail slide-over, its title has to appear on screen.
API4 -- ...and its real title, which is Microsoft's own text and cannot be in the fixture.
API5 -- the first stat card's value, derived over the WHOLE corpus rather than the capped post list.
API6 -- the first density row's real workload name.
API7 -- the endpoint STATES that it has not read the tenant's configuration against these notices, rather than leaving the page to imply it did.
API8 -- the cap is REPORTED rather than silent, so a reader can tell a short post list from a quiet tenant.

API9 -- SECURITY: a ?customerId= pointed at ANOTHER tenant (customer 3, which really does hold its own Message Center items) still returns THIS customer's scoped payload. The param is not read at all -- the route source contains no req.query -- so it cannot select a tenant the way /api/msp/message-center's param does. NOTE: `value` does not interpolate {{vars}} in this harness, so this asserts the scope flag rather than re-asserting the item count; the count itself is pinned against the DOM in MSC5.
